title: Endpoint DLP resources and resource tags: network shares, printers, removable storage, endpoint applications

prose.text: {{resource-types}} {{page-name-by-license}} {{endpoint-apps-account-team}} {{personal-cloud-built-in}} What Endpoint Context is and what it shows is in [[zia.endpoint-context]].

prose.label: Import and tags.
prose.text: {{csv-import}} {{csv-import-tags}} {{tags-replace-groups}} {{tags-by-licence-and-prebuilt}} The API and Terraform names for these objects are in [[zia.dlp.endpoint-dlp]].
Whether these resources are the same objects as the device control resources is open in [[zia.dlp.endpoint-device-control]]. The rules that use them are in [[zia.dlp.endpoint-rules]].

macos-description-limit.statement: In the Edit macOS Application drawer, the application Description cannot exceed 255 characters.

quotes: Description: (Optional) Enter additional notes or information about the application. The description cannot exceed 255 characters.

directory-paths-entry.statement: For a network share limited to listed directories, the Directory Paths field takes paths such as /<folder>/<subfolder> separated by line breaks.

quotes: Files in the following directories and subdirectories: Select this option if you want to specify the directories and subdirectories to be included. If you select this option, the Directory Paths field appears.
Add paths (e.g., /<folder>/<subfolder>) separated by line breaks, then click Add.

resource-types.statement: Creating a resource is the first step in setting up Endpoint DLP policies and in customizing Endpoint Context data. For Endpoint DLP, resources can be created for network shares, printers, removable storage devices, and applications; for Endpoint Context, application details can be specified.

quotes: Creating a resource is the first step in setting up Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies and in customizing Endpoint Context data for your organization.
For the former, you can create resources for network shares, printers, removable storage devices, and applications; for the latter, you can specify application details.

page-name-by-license.statement: The resources page is called DLP Resources if the organization has licensed only Endpoint DLP, Endpoint Resources if it has licensed only Endpoint Context, and DLP & Endpoint Resources if it has licensed both.

quotes: If your organization has licensed only Endpoint DLP, this page is called DLP Resources.
If your organization has licensed only Endpoint Context, this page is called Endpoint Resources.
If your organization has licensed both Endpoint DLP and Endpoint Context, this page is called DLP & Endpoint Resources.

endpoint-apps-account-team.statement: The DLP Resources page is available if the organization has licensed Endpoint DLP but not Endpoint Context, and on it the page says to contact the Zscaler Account team to access the feature.

quotes: The DLP Resources page is available if your organization has licensed Endpoint DLP but not Endpoint Context.

evidence.after: The DLP Resources page is available if your organization has licensed Endpoint DLP but not Endpoint Context.
quotes: To access this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.

personal-cloud-built-in.statement: The Zscaler service automatically supports Box, Dropbox, Google Drive, iCloud for macOS, and OneDrive personal cloud storage accounts, and no extra configuration is available for those services as DLP resources.

quotes: The Zscaler service automatically supports Box, Dropbox, Google Drive, iCloud for macOS, and OneDrive personal cloud storage accounts. No extra configuration is available for those services as DLP resources.

network-share-fields.statement: A network share's server entry can use regular expressions and CIDR ranges for advanced matching; the vendor's examples are regex:^(?i)srv* (all network servers starting with "srv", case-insensitive) and cidr:192.168.1.0/24. The share is scoped either to all files and directories on the server or to files in listed directories and subdirectories.

quotes: You can also use regular expressions and CIDR ranges for advanced matching. For example:
regex:^(?i)srv* (matches all network servers that start with "srv" and the match is case-insensitive)
cidr:192.168.1.0/24 (matches network servers with an IP address starting with "192.168.1")
All files and directories on this server: Select this option if you want to include all files and directories on the specified server.
Files in the following directories and subdirectories: Select this option if you want to specify the directories and subdirectories to be included.

printer-fields.statement: A printer resource takes a Domain (the name of the domain where the printer is located), a Printer Name (as it appears in the OS list of printers) and an IP Address.

quotes: Domain: Enter the name of the domain where the printer is located.
Printer Name: Enter the name of the printer as it appears in the OS list of printers.
IP Address: Enter the IP address for the printer.

removable-storage-fields.statement: A removable storage device resource needs at least one of the criteria Vendor ID (the manufacturer), Product ID or Serial Number.

quotes: Enter at least one of the following Criteria for the device:
Vendor ID: The manufacturer of the removable storage device
Product ID: The product ID of the removable storage device
Serial Number: The serial number of the removable storage device

application-fields.statement: The Windows application criteria are Original File Name (the original file name of the executable, located on the Details tab in the Properties for the executable file), File Name (the name of the executable that runs the application) and Digitally Signed. The macOS application criteria are Bundle ID (the bundle identifier that uniquely identifies the application), File Name and Digitally Signed. Digitally Signed is Any (no signature check), Yes (signature required) or No (signature not required) in the Windows drawer, whose application Description cannot exceed 255 characters.

quotes: Original File Name: Enter the original file name of the executable. This name is located on the Details tab in the Properties for the executable file in Windows.
File Name: Enter the name of the executable that runs the application.
Digitally Signed: Select an option for whether the application file must be digitally signed by a trusted provider:
Any: The Zscaler service does not check for a digital signature.
Yes: The Zscaler service requires a digital signature.
No: The Zscaler service does not require a digital signature.
The description cannot exceed 255 characters.
Bundle ID: Enter the bundle identifier that uniquely identifies the application.
File Name: Enter the name of the executable that runs the application.
Digitally Signed: Select an option for whether the application file must be digitally signed by a trusted provider:

application-types.statement: Endpoint applications are Well-Known (frequently seen in the Zero Trust Exchange security cloud, a dynamic classification), Discovered (found on endpoints by the Zscaler service) or Custom (added to a tenant by an administrator).

quotes: Well-Known: Applications that are frequently seen within the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) security cloud. This is a dynamic classification that includes more applications as they become more prevalent over time.
Discovered: Applications that are discovered on endpoints by the Zscaler service.
Custom: Applications added to a tenant by an administrator.

application-risk-level.statement: Endpoint Application Risk Level is the calculated risk level of an application based on multiple properties and behaviors, and it can change based on the latest data. The service uses four risk levels; all applications might initially appear as Unknown until risk identification is complete. Applications identified as Discovered or Well-Known cannot be deleted.

quotes: Endpoint Application Risk Level: The calculated risk level of the application based on multiple properties and behaviors, including static and dynamic properties of the application. Risk is an independent property and can change based on the latest data.
The Zscaler service uses four risk levels:
Unknown: All applications might initially appear as an unknown risk until the risk identification and quantification process by the Zscaler service is complete.
You cannot delete applications identified as Discovered or Well-Known by the Zscaler service.

application-edit-and-override.statement: Options can be configured for custom applications but most options can only be viewed for well-known applications and applications discovered by the Zscaler service. Version and Application Risk Level are not editable, but Application Risk Level Override can be set to Unknown, Low, Medium, or High to override the risk level the service set.

quotes: You can configure options for custom applications but can only view most options for well-known applications (e.g., Zoom, Excel) and applications discovered by the Zscaler service.
Version: The version number of the endpoint application. This field is not editable.
Application Risk Level: The risk level for the application, based on analysis by the Zscaler service. This field is not editable.
Application Risk Level Override: Select an option (i.e., Unknown, Low, Medium, or High) to override the risk level for the application set by the Zscaler service.

csv-import.statement: Multiple resources can be imported at once from a CSV file, with a sample template available to download for each resource type; importing multiple applications is not supported. The row formats shown are <name>,<description>,<server name>,<paths>; <name>,<description>,<UNC>,<IP address>,<domain>; and <name>,<description>,<vendor ID>,<product ID>,<serial number>.

quotes: You can import multiple resources at the same time using a CSV file. There is a sample template available to download for each resource type.
The Zscaler service doesn't support importing multiple applications.
<name>,<description>,<server name>,<paths>
<name>,<description>,<UNC>,<IP address>,<domain>
<name>,<description>,<vendor ID>,<product ID>,<serial number>

csv-import-tags.statement: In the network share import, the imported resources can be added to a new tag (New Tag, with a name and description) or to an existing tag selected from the Select Tag drop-down menu.

quotes: To add the resources to a new tag, click New Tag, then specify a name and description for the tag.
To add the resources to an existing tag, click Existing Tag, then select a group from the Select Tag drop-down menu.

tags-replace-groups.statement: For Endpoint DLP, resource groups are replaced by resource tags: groups already configured are automatically converted to resource tag groups, and policies that used resource groups are automatically updated to use the converted resource tag groups. Grouping resources lets Endpoint DLP policy rules apply to multiple resources at the same time.

quotes: Resource groups are replaced by resource tags for Endpoint DLP. Any resource groups that you have already configured are automatically converted to resource tag groups. All policies that previously used resource groups are automatically updated to use the converted resource tag groups.
Grouping DLP & Endpoint resources allows you to apply Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy rules to multiple resources at the same time.
Resource groups are replaced by resource tags for Endpoint DLP. Any resource groups that you have already configured are automatically converted to resource tag groups.

tags-by-licence-and-prebuilt.statement: If the organization has licensed Endpoint Context but not Endpoint DLP, it cannot create tags for network shares, network printers, or removable storage devices. The Endpoint Application Tags tab contains both prebuilt lists of applications by category or theme from Zscaler, such as “Certificate Pinned” or “AI Browsers”, and custom application lists, and Edit can be clicked on an existing customized prebuilt list.

quotes: If your organization has licensed Endpoint Context but not Endpoint DLP, you do not have the option to create tags for network shares, network printers, or removable storage devices.

The Endpoint Application Tags tab contains both prebuilt lists of applications by category or theme from Zscaler, such as “Certificate Pinned” or “AI Browsers”, but can also contain custom application lists specific to your organization.
You can click Edit on an existing customized prebuilt list.
